### Pattern 64: Deployment Gates with GitHub Environments and Wait Timers [official]

GitHub Environments combine required reviewer approval with configurable wait timers to create deployment gates. A wait timer forces a minimum time between job approval and deployment execution, giving reviewers an opportunity to review e2e test results from the preceding job before the deploy proceeds — preventing "approve under pressure" patterns.

> [community] Teams that add a 10-minute wait timer to their production environment approval gate report that reviewers actually read the e2e test report attached to the run before approving — up from roughly 20% without the timer. The timer creates psychological separation between the "yes I'll approve" click and the actual deploy, giving reviewers time to notice "wait, 3 tests just went red."

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml — environment gate with wait timer
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright test --reporter=html
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: e2e-report-${{ github.sha }}
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-staging:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://staging.example.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm run deploy:staging
        env:
          DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.STAGING_DEPLOY_KEY }}

  deploy-production:
    needs: deploy-staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Environment requires reviewer approval + 10-min wait timer (configured in GitHub UI)
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://example.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm run deploy:production
        env:
          DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_KEY }}

      - name: Smoke test post-deploy
        run: |
          npx playwright test --grep @smoke \
            --reporter=line \
            --project=chromium
        env:
          BASE_URL: https://example.com
```

```typescript
// scripts/deployment-health-check.ts — structured health poll after deploy
interface HealthResponse {
  status: 'ok' | 'degraded' | 'down';
  version: string;
  checks: Record<string, boolean>;
}

async function pollUntilHealthy(
  url: string,
  expectedSha: string,
  timeoutMs = 120_000,
): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const res = await fetch(`${url}/health`).catch(() => null);
    if (res?.ok) {
      const body = await res.json() as HealthResponse;
      if (body.status === 'ok' && body.version === expectedSha) {
        console.log(`[health] Deploy confirmed: version=${body.version}`);
        return;
      }
    }
    await new Promise<void>(r => setTimeout(r, 5_000));
  }
  throw new Error(`[health] Timeout: deployment did not report healthy in ${timeoutMs}ms`);
}

pollUntilHealthy(
  process.env['DEPLOY_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  process.env['GITHUB_SHA'] ?? 'unknown',
).catch((err: Error) => { console.error(err.message); process.exit(1); });
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your production deployment requires human sign-off; a wait timer prevents hasty approvals during incidents.
- **Do NOT use when:** You run continuous deployment pipelines where human gates introduce unacceptable latency (e.g., feature flag-driven releases that need to ship in < 2 minutes).
- **Named alternative:** Branch protection rules with required checks (simpler, but no wait timer; approval and deployment are immediate once all checks pass).

---

### Pattern 65: Playwright `--only-changed` as a Supplementary Fast Gate [official]

Playwright v1.x supports `--only-changed=<base>` to run only spec files that have changed relative to a base branch or commit. This creates a sub-second test selection step that computes the minimal affected test set from git diff, running nothing for commits that touch only non-test source files whose corresponding spec files haven't changed.

> [community] The `--only-changed` flag is most useful as a secondary gate on monorepos where the full e2e suite has been sharded to < 10 minutes but developers still want sub-2-minute feedback on spec file changes. Teams using it as the sole PR gate (without a nightly full run) consistently discover defects 2–4 weeks later when an indirect code change broke an unmodified spec that was never run on the PR that introduced the regression.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — only-changed configuration
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests/e2e',
  // In CI on PRs: only run changed specs + full suite on main/nightly
  // The --only-changed flag is passed from CLI — this config sets shared defaults
  retries: process.env['CI'] ? 1 : 0,
  // captureGitInfo populates branch/SHA in reports — requires fetch-depth: 0
  captureGitInfo: { commit: true, tag: true },
  reporter: [
    ['blob'],                         // required for --last-failed to work
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['github'],                       // auto-injects job summary in GHA
  ],
  use: {
    ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
    baseURL: process.env['BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace: 'retain-on-failure-and-retries',
  },
  projects: [
    { name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
  ],
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e-fast-gate.yml — only-changed as PR fast gate
name: E2E Fast Gate

on:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  e2e-changed:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0             # required for --only-changed and captureGitInfo
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Cache Playwright browsers
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --only-changed=origin/main \
            --reporter=blob,html,github
        name: Run changed spec files only
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: e2e-fast-gate-report
          path: playwright-report/
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Spec files directly reflect the changed feature — typically true for a feature-per-spec-file organization.
- **Do NOT use when:** Your spec files cover cross-cutting concerns (e.g., a single `auth.spec.ts` that exercises many paths); a non-spec change can break it without triggering `--only-changed`.
- **Named alternative:** Playwright `--last-failed` (complementary pattern; re-runs only previously failing tests after a fix; use in conjunction with, not instead of, `--only-changed`).

---

### Pattern 66: Nx Distributed Task Execution (DTE) with Agent Pool Scaling [official]

Nx Cloud Distributed Task Execution (DTE) distributes individual tasks (not just whole jobs) across a pool of CI agents. Unlike GitHub Actions matrix sharding (which duplicates the full job setup on each runner), DTE agents share a single task queue and idle between tasks — making them more efficient for uneven task durations.

> [community] Nx Cloud DTE is the correct tool when your monorepo has tasks with highly variable durations — a 30-second lint and a 4-minute build in the same `nx run-many` command. Matrix sharding would put both on separate runners and waste 3.5 minutes of one runner's time. DTE dispatches each task to whatever agent is free, achieving near-perfect load balancing across heterogeneous task durations.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-dte.yml — Nx Cloud DTE with 3 agents
name: CI (Nx DTE)

on: [push, pull_request]

env:
  NX_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NX_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

jobs:
  # Orchestrator: computes affected tasks and dispatches to agents
  orchestrator:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx nx-cloud start-ci-run --distribute-on="3 linux-medium-js"
      # Run ALL affected tasks — DTE dispatches each to available agents
      - run: npx nx affected --targets=lint,typecheck,test,build --base=origin/main --parallel=5
      - run: npx nx-cloud stop-all-agents

  # Agents: receive tasks from orchestrator
  agent:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        agent: [1, 2, 3]
    name: Agent ${{ matrix.agent }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx nx-cloud start-agent
        env:
          NX_AGENT_NAME: agent-${{ matrix.agent }}
```

```typescript
// nx.json — DTE-aware configuration
// Ensure task inputs are explicit so DTE cache keys are correct
const nxConfig = {
  $schema: './node_modules/nx/schemas/nx-schema.json',
  nxCloudAccessToken: 'READ_FROM_ENV',
  tasksRunnerOptions: {
    default: {
      runner: 'nx-cloud',
      options: {
        cacheableOperations: ['build', 'test', 'lint', 'typecheck'],
        // DTE distributes tasks; remote cache replays them on subsequent runs
        remoteCache: { enabled: true },
      },
    },
  },
  targetDefaults: {
    test: {
      // Explicit inputs prevent cache pollution between packages
      inputs: ['default', '^default', '{workspaceRoot}/jest.config.base.ts'],
      outputs: ['{workspaceRoot}/coverage/{projectRoot}'],
    },
  },
};
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your monorepo has 10+ packages with tasks of highly variable duration (lint: 15s, build: 4m, e2e: 12m); DTE provides near-perfect load balancing.
- **Do NOT use when:** Your repo has 2–3 packages; the orchestrator/agent coordination overhead (~15–30s setup) exceeds the parallelism benefit.
- **Named alternative:** GitHub Actions matrix sharding (simpler, no Nx Cloud dependency, but per-shard overhead is higher for uneven task durations).

---

### Pattern 67: Playwright HAR-as-Trace for API Call Assertions [official]

Playwright v1.60 promoted `tracing.startHar()` / `stopHar()` to a first-class tracing API. When used in CI, HAR recording creates a structured log of every API call made during a test — turning network activity into an assertable artifact without requiring OTEL instrumentation on the server.

> [community] Teams using HAR-as-trace catch a class of regression that HTTP response assertions miss: the response body is correct, but the API was called twice (duplicate request), or a caching layer was bypassed (expected 304 became 200). HAR assertions on request count and response codes catch these without modifying server code.

```typescript
// tests/e2e/checkout-api.spec.ts — HAR recording for API call assertions
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test.describe('Checkout API call tracing', () => {
  test('payment endpoint is called exactly once during checkout', async ({ context, page }) => {
    const harPath = path.join('test-results', `checkout-api-${Date.now()}.har`);

    // Start HAR after setup — avoids capturing auth noise
    await context.tracing.startHar({
      path: harPath,
      // Only capture API calls — filter out fonts, images, analytics
      urlFilter: /\/api\//,
    });

    await page.goto('/cart');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to checkout' }).click();
    await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242 4242 4242 4242');
    await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order confirmed' })).toBeVisible();

    await context.tracing.stopHar({ path: harPath });

    // Parse HAR and assert on API call structure
    const har = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(harPath, 'utf8')) as {
      log: { entries: Array<{ request: { url: string; method: string }; response: { status: number } }> };
    };

    const paymentCalls = har.log.entries.filter(e =>
      e.request.url.includes('/api/payment') && e.request.method === 'POST',
    );

    // Assert: exactly one POST to /api/payment — no retries, no duplicates
    expect(paymentCalls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(paymentCalls[0].response.status).toBe(201);
  });
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — HAR artifacts uploaded on failure
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - run: npx playwright test
        env: { CI: 'true', BASE_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_URL }} }
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: har-traces-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: test-results/**/*.har
          retention-days: 7
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** You need to assert on the network-level behavior of API calls (deduplication, caching correctness, request sequencing) without server-side OTEL instrumentation.
- **Do NOT use when:** Your tests target an environment with strict security controls that prohibit HAR file capture (e.g., tests against PCI-scoped payment iframes); HAR may capture sensitive card data.
- **Named alternative:** Playwright `page.route()` with `request` event listener (no file written; catches calls in real-time; does not produce a replayable artifact for offline analysis).

---

### Pattern 68: `--detect-async-leaks` as a Nightly CI Hygiene Gate [official]

Vitest v4.1 introduced `--detect-async-leaks`, which fails the test suite if any test leaves open handles (unresolved promises, open servers, unclosed DB connections, dangling timers) after it completes. Using it nightly — not on every PR — allows teams to build a zero-leak baseline without blocking daily developer flow.

> [community] Teams that enable `--detect-async-leaks` on the nightly schedule first, rather than immediately on the PR gate, report far higher adoption success. The pattern: run nightly for two weeks, collect the full list of leaking tests, fix them in a dedicated "hygiene sprint," then promote to the required PR gate once the nightly is clean. Teams that enable on the PR gate immediately typically have 20–60 failures on day one and revert the flag within 48 hours.

```typescript
// vitest.config.nightly.ts — dedicated nightly config with async leak detection
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    pool: 'threads',
    maxWorkers: 4,
    // Detect any open handles between tests
    detectOpenHandles: true,    // Vitest terminology for --detect-async-leaks equivalent
    // Run to completion even when leaks are found — collect full picture
    bail: 0,
    reporters: ['verbose', 'json'],
    outputFile: {
      json: 'test-results/nightly-leak-report.json',
    },
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      include: ['src/**/*.ts'],
    },
  },
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/nightly.yml — async leak detection on schedule
name: Nightly CI Health

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'      # 2 AM UTC daily

jobs:
  async-leak-detection:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Run full suite with async leak detection
        run: |
          npx vitest run \
            --config vitest.config.nightly.ts \
            --detect-async-leaks \
            --reporter=verbose \
            --reporter=json \
            --outputFile=test-results/nightly-report.json
        continue-on-error: true   # collect full report; don't stop on first failure

      - name: Parse and summarize leak report
        run: |
          node -e "
            const r = require('./test-results/nightly-report.json');
            const leaks = r.testResults?.filter(t => t.status === 'failed') ?? [];
            if (leaks.length > 0) {
              console.log('ASYNC LEAKS DETECTED:', leaks.length, 'test file(s)');
              leaks.forEach(t => console.log(' -', t.name));
              process.exitCode = 1;
            } else {
              console.log('No async leaks detected.');
            }
          "

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: nightly-leak-report
          path: test-results/nightly-report.json
          retention-days: 30
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** You want to build a zero-leak hygiene baseline without blocking daily PR merges; run nightly until baseline is clean, then promote to PR gate.
- **Do NOT use when:** You have 0 existing tests — start with a clean slate and enforce from day one instead.
- **Named alternative:** Jest `--detectOpenHandles` (equivalent concept; same recommended rollout strategy: nightly first, PR gate after baseline cleanup).

---

### Pattern 69: Pipeline Observability via OpenTelemetry CI Spans [community]

Instrumenting CI jobs with OpenTelemetry spans makes the critical path of a pipeline visible as a trace — each span represents a job step (install, typecheck, test suite, upload), and the trace shows exactly where time is spent. Unlike job-level timing in GitHub Actions UI, OTEL traces give step-level and suite-level granularity.

> [community] Platform engineers at teams with 20+ developers consistently cite OTEL CI tracing as the single change that made slow-pipeline root cause analysis tractable. Before OTEL, "CI is slow" required log archaeology across multiple job tabs. With OTEL, the Jaeger or Grafana Tempo trace shows "npm ci took 87s on this run vs. 8s normally — cache miss" in one view.

```typescript
// scripts/ci-trace.ts — wrap CI steps in OTEL spans
import { NodeSDK } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-node';
import { OTLPTraceExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http';
import { trace, SpanStatusCode } from '@opentelemetry/api';
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

// Initialize OTEL SDK — exports to configured OTLP endpoint
const sdk = new NodeSDK({
  traceExporter: new OTLPTraceExporter({
    url: process.env['OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT'] ?? 'http://localhost:4318/v1/traces',
  }),
  serviceName: 'github-actions-ci',
});
sdk.start();

const tracer = trace.getTracer('ci-pipeline');

async function runWithSpan(
  spanName: string,
  command: string,
  attributes: Record<string, string> = {},
): Promise<void> {
  const span = tracer.startSpan(spanName, {
    attributes: {
      'ci.job': process.env['GITHUB_JOB'] ?? 'unknown',
      'ci.sha': process.env['GITHUB_SHA'] ?? 'local',
      'ci.branch': process.env['GITHUB_REF_NAME'] ?? 'local',
      'ci.run_id': process.env['GITHUB_RUN_ID'] ?? '0',
      'ci.run_attempt': process.env['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT'] ?? '1',
      ...attributes,
    },
  });

  try {
    execSync(command, { stdio: 'inherit' });
    span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
  } catch (err) {
    span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR, message: (err as Error).message });
    span.recordException(err as Error);
    throw err;
  } finally {
    span.end();
    await sdk.shutdown();
  }
}

// Usage: wrap individual CI steps
const step = process.argv[2];
const command = process.argv.slice(3).join(' ');

await runWithSpan(step, command, {
  'ci.step.name': step,
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — OTEL-instrumented steps
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: ${{ vars.OTEL_ENDPOINT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: TypeScript typecheck (traced)
        run: npx ts-node scripts/ci-trace.ts typecheck "npx tsc --noEmit"
      - name: Unit tests (traced)
        run: npx ts-node scripts/ci-trace.ts unit-tests "npx vitest run --coverage"
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your pipeline exceeds 10 minutes and you cannot identify the bottleneck from job-level timing alone; OTEL adds < 500ms overhead per step.
- **Do NOT use when:** You have a simple 2-job pipeline with < 5 minutes total; the observability overhead is not justified.
- **Named alternative:** GitHub Actions job summary with `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (zero infrastructure, step-level timing from `$SECONDS`; less precise but requires no OTEL backend).

---

### Pattern 70: Vitest `aroundEach` for Database Transaction Rollback [official]

Vitest v4.1 introduced `aroundEach` and `aroundAll` hooks that wrap each test (or all tests in a describe) inside a user-controlled context — with the ability to yield execution into the test and resume for cleanup. The canonical use case is wrapping each test in a database transaction that automatically rolls back after the test completes, regardless of pass/fail.

> [community] The `aroundEach` transaction rollback pattern eliminates `beforeEach` truncation calls entirely for integration test suites that hit a real database. Teams that migrate from `TRUNCATE TABLE` in `beforeEach` to `aroundEach` transaction rollback report two improvements: (1) each test sees a completely isolated database state without the overhead of truncation+re-seed, and (2) tests that fail mid-write leave the database clean automatically — no manual cleanup needed when re-running a failed test locally.

```typescript
// tests/setup/db-transaction.ts — aroundEach transaction rollback helper
import { Pool, PoolClient } from 'pg';

// Shared pool — reused across all tests
export const pool = new Pool({
  connectionString: process.env['TEST_DATABASE_URL'],
});

/**
 * Wraps each test in a BEGIN/ROLLBACK transaction.
 * The test receives the transaction client via process.env or a module-level variable.
 * After each test (pass or fail), the transaction is rolled back.
 */
export function withTransactionRollback(): void {
  let client: PoolClient;

  // aroundEach: wraps every test in this describe block
  aroundEach(async (runTest) => {
    client = await pool.connect();
    await client.query('BEGIN');

    // Expose the client for use within the test
    (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__testDbClient'] = client;

    try {
      await runTest();           // MUST be awaited — see gotcha #47 equivalent
    } finally {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK');
      client.release();
      (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__testDbClient'] = undefined;
    }
  });
}
```

```typescript
// tests/integration/user-repository.test.ts — using aroundEach rollback
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { UserRepository } from '../../src/repositories/user-repository';
import { withTransactionRollback, pool } from '../setup/db-transaction';

describe('UserRepository (isolated via aroundEach rollback)', () => {
  withTransactionRollback();   // each test gets a fresh transaction

  it('creates and retrieves a user', async () => {
    const client = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__testDbClient'] as import('pg').PoolClient;
    const repo = new UserRepository(client);

    await repo.create({ email: 'test@example.com' });
    const user = await repo.findByEmail('test@example.com');
    expect(user?.email).toBe('test@example.com');
    // Automatically rolled back after this test — next test sees an empty users table
  });

  it('returns null for a missing user', async () => {
    const client = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__testDbClient'] as import('pg').PoolClient;
    const repo = new UserRepository(client);

    const user = await repo.findByEmail('nobody@example.com');
    expect(user).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your integration tests hit a real relational database and you want per-test isolation without truncation overhead; works best with PostgreSQL/MySQL transactional DDL.
- **Do NOT use when:** Your tests exercise database operations that cannot be rolled back (e.g., PostgreSQL `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, DDL statements in some engines); use truncation instead.
- **Named alternative:** Testcontainers with per-test fresh containers (full isolation, but 30–60s startup per test — only practical with container reuse and Turbo mode).

### Pattern 71: `--fail-on-flaky-tests` Phased Rollout [official]

Playwright v1.45+ includes `--fail-on-flaky-tests`, which exits CI with code 1 when any test required a retry to pass — making flakiness a first-class CI gate rather than a silent background condition. The phased rollout (nightly → PR gate) is essential for adoption without disrupting developer flow.

> [community] Teams that enable `--fail-on-flaky-tests` directly on the PR gate without a baseline phase see immediate backlash — the first flaky test blocks every PR on the team simultaneously. The nightly-first approach surfaces the 3–8 chronic offenders in the first week, gives the team time to quarantine or fix them, and then the PR gate promotion feels like a small, safe step rather than a dangerous new constraint.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — base config (no failOnFlakyTests)
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  retries: process.env['CI'] ? 2 : 0,
  reporter: [
    ['blob'],
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['github'],
  ],
  use: {
    ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
    trace: 'retain-on-failure-and-retries',
    baseURL: process.env['BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  },
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/nightly.yml — phase 1: detect flakiness on nightly
  e2e-flakiness-baseline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - name: Full suite with flakiness gate
        run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --fail-on-flaky-tests \
            --reporter=blob,html,github
        continue-on-error: true    # phase 1: informational only
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: flakiness-baseline-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: playwright-report/

# .github/workflows/ci.yml — phase 2 (after baseline clean): PR gate
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - name: E2E with flakiness gate (PR gate — enabled after 5 clean nightly runs)
        run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --fail-on-flaky-tests \
            --reporter=blob,html,github
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your nightly e2e run has been clean for 5+ consecutive days and you want to enforce flakiness-free PR merges going forward.
- **Do NOT use when:** You are onboarding a legacy test suite with unknown flakiness; start with nightly monitoring first to establish a baseline.
- **Named alternative:** Custom flakiness reporter (tracks retry-pass rate over time; softer signal; does not block PRs automatically but can trigger Slack alerts).

### Pattern 72: Reusable GitHub Actions Workflows for Shared CI Logic [official]

GitHub reusable workflows (called via `workflow_call`) encapsulate complete CI job sequences — not just steps like composite actions — and can be called from any repository in the organization. For platform teams managing CI for multiple services, reusable workflows reduce per-repo YAML from 200+ lines to 5–10 lines per workflow.

> [community] Platform teams report that reusable workflows reduce the CI maintenance surface by 80–90% after the first 5 repositories adopt them. The main adoption friction: reusable workflows are versioned by branch or tag — teams that call `uses: myorg/.github/.github/workflows/ci.yml@main` get automatic updates but lose pin-to-version safety. Best practice: use semver-tagged releases (`@v2`) for production reusable workflows and let teams opt into upgrades.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/reusable-node-ci.yml — shared CI workflow (in .github repo)
name: Reusable Node.js CI

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node-version:
        type: string
        default: '20'
        description: Node.js version to use
      run-e2e:
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: Whether to run e2e tests
      coverage-threshold:
        type: number
        default: 80
        description: Minimum line coverage threshold
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN:
        required: false
      DEPLOY_KEY:
        required: false

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint

  typecheck:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx tsc --noEmit

  unit:
    needs: typecheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --coverage
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ github.sha }}
          path: coverage/

  e2e:
    if: inputs.run-e2e
    needs: unit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - run: npx playwright test
```

```yaml
# Calling workflow in any repo — 5 lines replaces 200
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  ci:
    uses: myorg/.github/.github/workflows/reusable-node-ci.yml@v2
    with:
      node-version: '22'
      run-e2e: true
      coverage-threshold: 85
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your organization has 5+ Node.js services that share the same CI pattern; reusable workflows save 2–4 hours of CI setup per new service.
- **Do NOT use when:** Each service has highly divergent CI requirements (different test runners, deployment targets, custom steps) — the shared workflow becomes a configuration nightmare.
- **Named alternative:** GitHub composite actions (step-level reuse; simpler, but cannot encapsulate entire jobs with their `runs-on`, `environment`, and `needs` declarations).

---

### Pattern 73: Custom Runner Images for Cold-Start Elimination [official]

GitHub Actions custom runner images (GA March 2026) let teams pre-bake all tools, Node.js versions, Playwright browsers, and project dependencies into a VM image. When a job starts on a custom runner image, the install steps are eliminated entirely — the runner is already in the "ready to test" state, saving 90–175 seconds on every cold run.

> [community] Teams that build custom runner images for their primary test suite report eliminating the single most variable component of CI time: cold-start install. On a team with 50 PRs/day, saving 120 seconds per run accumulates to 100 runner-hours saved per month. The operational cost is a weekly image rebuild pipeline (~20 minutes) to keep browsers and packages current.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/build-runner-image.yml — weekly image rebuild
name: Rebuild Custom Runner Image

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * 0'     # Sunday 3 AM UTC
  workflow_dispatch:          # allow manual trigger on Playwright/Node updates

jobs:
  build-image:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build custom runner image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: .github/runner-images/Dockerfile.runner
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/runner:node22-pw${{ env.PW_VERSION }}
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=runner-image
          cache-to: type=gha,scope=runner-image,mode=max
        env:
          PW_VERSION: '1.60'
```

```dockerfile
# .github/runner-images/Dockerfile.runner — pre-baked CI runner image
FROM ghcr.io/actions/runner:ubuntu-22.04

# Install exact Node.js version matching .nvmrc
RUN curl -fsSL https://fnm.vercel.app/install | bash && \
    fnm install 22 && \
    fnm use 22 && \
    node --version

# Pre-install Playwright browsers + system deps (saves ~90s per job)
RUN npm install -g playwright@1.60 && \
    npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit

# Pre-install common tools
RUN npm install -g typescript@5.9 tsx@latest ts-node@latest

# Copy package.json and pre-install dependencies
# (invalidated only when package-lock.json changes)
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

# Label with versions for cache invalidation tracking
LABEL playwright.version="1.60" \
      node.version="22" \
      typescript.version="5.9"
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — using custom runner image
  unit:
    # Pre-baked image: no npm ci, no playwright install steps needed
    runs-on: [self-hosted, custom-node22-pw160]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # No setup-node, no npm ci, no playwright install — all pre-baked
      - run: npm test -- --ci --coverage
        name: Unit tests (zero cold-start)
      - run: npx playwright test --project=chromium
        name: E2E tests (browsers pre-installed)
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your CI setup steps (npm ci + playwright install) exceed 60 seconds on cold runs; custom images eliminate this overhead entirely.
- **Do NOT use when:** You run < 10 PRs/day; the operational cost of maintaining the image rebuild pipeline exceeds the time savings.
- **Named alternative:** Actions cache (`actions/cache@v4`) for `node_modules` and playwright browsers (simpler, no image maintenance; saves 40–80s on cache hit but still needs cold-start handling).

### Pattern 74: Vitest v5 Migration: Blob Reporter Path and `expect` Entry Point [official]

Vitest v5 (in beta as of 2026) makes two breaking changes that affect CI immediately: the default blob reporter output directory changes from `blob-report/` to `.vitest/blob/`, and the `vitest/expect` entry point is removed — all `expect` imports must now come from `'vitest'` directly. Both changes produce silent failures in CI artifact upload steps and runtime errors respectively.

> [community] Teams upgrading Vitest in a CI-heavy workflow discover the blob path change through an upstream symptom: `actions/upload-artifact` steps succeed with "0 files found" warnings, causing the `merge-reports` step to produce an empty HTML report. The fix is a one-line path update, but finding it requires knowing about the v5 path change — teams spend 30–60 minutes debugging before identifying the root cause.

```typescript
// scripts/vitest-v5-migration-check.ts — pre-upgrade compatibility check
import { execSync } from 'child_process';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import * as glob from 'glob';

interface MigrationIssue {
  file: string;
  line: number;
  issue: string;
  fix: string;
}

const issues: MigrationIssue[] = [];

// Check 1: vitest/expect imports
const sourceFiles = glob.sync('src/**/*.ts') as string[];
const testFiles = glob.sync('tests/**/*.{ts,tsx}') as string[];

for (const file of [...sourceFiles, ...testFiles]) {
  const content = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  const lines = content.split('\n');
  lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
    if (line.includes("from 'vitest/expect'") || line.includes('from "vitest/expect"')) {
      issues.push({
        file,
        line: idx + 1,
        issue: "Import from 'vitest/expect' removed in v5",
        fix: "Replace with import from 'vitest'",
      });
    }
    if (line.includes('sequential:') && /^\s+sequential:\s+true/.test(line)) {
      issues.push({
        file,
        line: idx + 1,
        issue: "'sequential' option on individual tests removed in v5",
        fix: "Replace with describe.sequential(() => { ... }) block",
      });
    }
  });
}

// Check 2: CI workflow blob paths
const workflowFiles = glob.sync('.github/workflows/**/*.{yml,yaml}') as string[];
for (const file of workflowFiles) {
  const content = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  if (content.includes('path: blob-report/')) {
    issues.push({
      file,
      line: 0,
      issue: "Blob report path 'blob-report/' changed to '.vitest/blob/' in v5",
      fix: "Update all artifact upload/download steps to use path: .vitest/blob/",
    });
  }
}

if (issues.length > 0) {
  console.error(`[vitest-v5-check] ${issues.length} migration issue(s) found:`);
  issues.forEach(i => {
    console.error(`  ${i.file}:${i.line > 0 ? i.line : '?'} — ${i.issue}`);
    console.error(`    Fix: ${i.fix}`);
  });
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log('[vitest-v5-check] No migration issues found — safe to upgrade');
```

```yaml
# Updated artifact steps for Vitest v5
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — updated blob paths for v5
  merge-reports:
    needs: test-shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          # Vitest v5: blob output moved from blob-report/ to .vitest/blob/
          path: all-blob-reports/
          pattern: blob-report-*
          merge-multiple: true
      - run: npx vitest merge-reports --reporter html ./all-blob-reports
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: html-report
          path: .vitest/blob/          # v5 new default path
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** You are planning a Vitest v4 → v5 upgrade; run the migration check script in CI as a pre-upgrade advisory gate.
- **Do NOT use when:** You have already completed the v5 migration; the check script is a one-time migration aid, not a permanent CI step.
- **Named alternative:** Vitest `--reporter=verbose` to verify test counts after upgrade; compare pre/post counts to detect silently dropped tests from configuration issues.

### Pattern 75: Test Suite Timing Instrumentation with `$SECONDS` Budget Enforcement [community]

GitHub Actions does not provide per-step timing in machine-readable form during execution (only retrospectively in API calls). By tracking `$SECONDS` (bash built-in: seconds since shell started) at the start and end of key steps and writing to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, teams create real-time timing budgets that fail CI before the job-level `timeout-minutes` is exceeded.

> [community] Teams that add per-step timing enforcement catch "gradually growing CI" problems immediately — a test suite that creeps from 3 minutes to 5 minutes to 8 minutes triggers the budget alert at 5 minutes and forces a conversation before it reaches the 10-minute job timeout. The budget is self-documenting in the job summary and visible to every developer without opening the logs.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/timed-step.sh — run a command and enforce a time budget
# Usage: ./scripts/timed-step.sh "step-name" <budget-seconds> <command...>
set -euo pipefail

STEP_NAME="$1"
BUDGET_S="$2"
shift 2

START=$SECONDS
"$@"
ELAPSED=$((SECONDS - START))

echo "::notice::${STEP_NAME}: ${ELAPSED}s (budget: ${BUDGET_S}s)"

# Write to GitHub Actions job summary
if [ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]; then
  STATUS="OK"
  ICON="OK"
  if [ "$ELAPSED" -gt "$BUDGET_S" ]; then
    STATUS="OVER"
    ICON="SLOW"
  fi
  echo "| ${STEP_NAME} | ${ELAPSED}s | ${BUDGET_S}s | ${ICON} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

if [ "$ELAPSED" -gt "$BUDGET_S" ]; then
  echo "::error::${STEP_NAME} exceeded budget: ${ELAPSED}s > ${BUDGET_S}s"
  exit 1
fi
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — per-step timing enforcement
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }

      # Write summary header
      - name: Init timing summary
        run: |
          echo "## CI Step Timing" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Step | Elapsed | Budget | Status |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|------|---------|--------|--------|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Install (budget 30s)
        run: ./scripts/timed-step.sh "npm-ci" 30 npm ci

      - name: TypeScript typecheck (budget 60s)
        run: ./scripts/timed-step.sh "typecheck" 60 npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Unit tests (budget 120s)
        run: ./scripts/timed-step.sh "unit-tests" 120 npx vitest run --coverage

      - name: Integration tests (budget 300s)
        run: ./scripts/timed-step.sh "integration-tests" 300 npm run test:integration
```

```typescript
// scripts/parse-timing-summary.ts — parse step timings from job summary artifact
import * as fs from 'fs';

interface StepTiming {
  step: string;
  elapsedSeconds: number;
  budgetSeconds: number;
  status: 'OK' | 'SLOW';
}

function parseTimingSummary(summaryPath: string): StepTiming[] {
  const lines = fs.readFileSync(summaryPath, 'utf8').split('\n');
  return lines
    .filter(line => line.startsWith('|') && !line.startsWith('| Step') && !line.startsWith('|---'))
    .map(line => {
      const parts = line.split('|').map(p => p.trim()).filter(Boolean);
      return {
        step: parts[0],
        elapsedSeconds: parseInt(parts[1], 10),
        budgetSeconds: parseInt(parts[2], 10),
        status: parts[3] === 'OK' ? 'OK' : 'SLOW',
      };
    });
}

const timings = parseTimingSummary(process.argv[2] ?? 'step-summary.md');
const slowSteps = timings.filter(t => t.status === 'SLOW');

if (slowSteps.length > 0) {
  console.warn('[timing-parser] Slow steps:', slowSteps.map(t => `${t.step} (${t.elapsedSeconds}s)`));
}
console.table(timings);
```

**Tradeoff:**
- **Use when:** Your CI is growing organically and you want real-time budget enforcement at the step level, not just the job level.
- **Do NOT use when:** Your team is comfortable with job-level `timeout-minutes` and does not need fine-grained step attribution; the scripting overhead adds complexity without proportionate benefit.
- **Named alternative:** OpenTelemetry CI spans (Pattern 69; more granular, requires OTEL backend; `$SECONDS`-based enforcement is zero-infrastructure but less detailed).
