### Vitest `coverage.changed` Guard for Non-PR Events

Vitest 4.1's `coverage.changed` option restricts coverage reporting to files changed since a base branch, reducing CI coverage computation from O(all files) to O(changed files). However, it silently falls back to an empty diff (showing 100% coverage on zero files) when `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is empty — which happens on `push` to `main`, `merge_group` events, and scheduled runs. The guard pattern below ensures full coverage runs on merge-to-main while enabling fast delta coverage on PRs.

> [community] A team using `coverage.changed: process.env['GITHUB_BASE_REF']` on all events found their main-branch coverage badge displayed "100%" because the merge-to-main push run had no base ref, resulting in zero changed files and an empty coverage report. The fix (guard the option to PR events only) also revealed that 23% of their codebase had no test coverage at all — invisible because only PR-level delta coverage had been reported for months.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — coverage.changed guard for PR-only delta coverage
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

// Determine if this is a PR run (GITHUB_BASE_REF is set on pull_request events)
const isPullRequest = Boolean(process.env['GITHUB_BASE_REF']);

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      reporter: ['text', 'lcov', 'html'],

      // Restrict to changed files only on PR — avoids full-suite coverage
      // computation on every file. Full coverage runs on main/merge queue.
      //
      // IMPORTANT: requires fetch-depth: 0 in actions/checkout.
      // Without full git history, git diff cannot compute changed files.
      changed: isPullRequest ? process.env['GITHUB_BASE_REF'] : false,

      // Always include explicit coverage thresholds for merge-to-main runs
      // where full coverage is computed.
      ...(isPullRequest ? {} : {
        thresholds: {
          lines: 80,
          branches: 75,
          functions: 80,
          statements: 80,
        },
      }),

      // Required in Vitest 4.x — 'all' option was removed
      include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
      exclude: ['src/**/*.d.ts', 'src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.spec.ts'],
    },
  },
});
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions — checkout with full history for coverage.changed
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0   # Required: full git history for git diff computation
      # Without this, GITHUB_BASE_REF exists but git cannot compute the diff,
      # causing coverage.changed to silently report zero changed files.
```

### Jest 30 `expect.arrayOf` and New Assertion APIs for CI Test Clarity

Jest 30 ships several new assertion APIs that reduce boilerplate in test cases and improve failure message readability — which matters in CI where developers diagnose failures from logs without a debugger. `expect.arrayOf` validates every element of an array against a matcher without a manual `.forEach` loop. `jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame()` simulates exactly one animation frame (16.67 ms) for testing `requestAnimationFrame`-based code without guessing the frame duration. The `using` keyword integration auto-restores spies when the block exits, eliminating forgotten `jest.restoreAllMocks()` calls that cause state leakage between tests.

> [community] Teams report that `expect.arrayOf` significantly improves API contract test legibility in CI failure logs. Previously, an array assertion failure showed `expected 150 to equal 200` with no context about which array element failed. With `expect.arrayOf(expect.objectContaining({status: 200}))`, the failure message shows the full mismatched element, cutting mean-time-to-diagnose from 8 minutes (reproduced locally) to under 2 minutes (readable from CI log).

```typescript
// src/__tests__/api-contract.test.ts — Jest 30 new assertion APIs
import { describe, test, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';

describe('GET /users', () => {
  test('returns array of valid user objects', async () => {
    const response = await fetch('/api/users');
    const users = await response.json();

    // expect.arrayOf (Jest 30+): validates every element against a matcher.
    // Failure message shows the specific element that failed, not just index.
    expect(users).toEqual(
      expect.arrayOf(
        expect.objectContaining({
          id: expect.any(Number),
          name: expect.any(String),
          email: expect.stringMatching(/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/),
          createdAt: expect.any(String),
        })
      )
    );
  });

  test('spy auto-restore with using keyword (Jest 30+)', () => {
    // The 'using' keyword auto-restores the spy when the block exits —
    // equivalent to calling jest.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach, but scoped
    // to exactly this test. No risk of spy state leaking to the next test.
    using fetchSpy = jest.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(
      new Response(JSON.stringify([{ id: 1, name: 'Alice' }]), { status: 200 })
    );

    // fetchSpy is restored automatically at end of this test block
    expect(fetchSpy).toBeDefined();
  });

  test('animation frame timer (Jest 30+)', () => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
    const callback = jest.fn();

    requestAnimationFrame(callback);

    // Advance exactly one 60fps frame (16.67ms) — no magic number required
    jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame();

    expect(callback).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    jest.useRealTimers();
  });
});
```

### Environment Parity: `.env.test` + `dotenv-flow` Injection Pattern

Environment parity failures (tests pass locally, fail in CI) most commonly stem from environment variables that developers set locally but forget to configure in CI. The `dotenv-flow` pattern loads environment-specific `.env.*` files in a defined priority order: `.env.test.local` (gitignored, local overrides) → `.env.test` (committed, CI defaults) → `.env` (base). With this setup, CI runners load only committed values from `.env.test`, while local developers can override specific variables via `.env.test.local` without affecting CI behavior.

> [community] A team with a 6-developer codebase had 3 different values for `TEST_TIMEOUT_MS` across developer machines — one developer had set it globally in their shell profile. Tests that timed out reliably in CI passed locally for two developers and failed non-deterministically for a third. After adopting `.env.test` with a committed `TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=10000`, all environments aligned and the non-deterministic failures disappeared. The shell-profile global was the root cause — invisible without the `.env.test` baseline.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — dotenv-flow integration for environment parity
import { defineConfig, loadEnv } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => {
  // Load .env, .env.test, .env.test.local in priority order.
  // CI only has .env.test (committed). Local devs can add .env.test.local.
  // This ensures CI and local environments share the same defaults.
  const env = loadEnv(mode, process.cwd(), '');

  return {
    test: {
      // Inject the loaded env into the test process
      env,

      // Hard-code the mode to 'test' regardless of CI env vars
      // so that .env.test is always loaded, not .env.production
      environment: 'node',

      // Prevent tests from reading REAL credentials from the runner environment
      // by listing allowed env vars explicitly. Any var not in this list
      // must be in .env.test to be available in tests.
      // (Opt-in: comment out if you need full runner env access)
      // passthrough: ['NODE_ENV', 'CI', 'GITHUB_SHA', 'GITHUB_REF'],
    },
  };
});
```

```
# .env.test — committed defaults for CI and developer baseline
# All developers and CI runners use these values unless locally overridden.
NODE_ENV=test
TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=10000
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000
LOG_LEVEL=warn

# .env.test.local — gitignored local overrides (NOT committed)
# Developers can override without affecting CI:
# BASE_URL=https://dev-alice.staging.example.com
# LOG_LEVEL=debug
```

### Playwright `tracing.startHar()` / `stopHar()` First-Class HAR Tracing

Playwright v1.60 promotes HAR recording from a `recordHar` context option to a first-class tracing API: `context.tracing.startHar(path)` / `context.tracing.stopHar()`. The new API integrates with `await using` for automatic cleanup, supports URL filtering to reduce HAR size in CI (where large HAR files inflate artifact storage costs), and allows HAR recording to start/stop mid-test — enabling before/after comparison of network traffic.

> [community] Teams using HAR recordings for API mocking in CI discovered that the old `recordHar` option captured all responses (including large binary responses like fonts and images) into HAR files that averaged 45 MB per test run. With `tracing.startHar()` and the `urlFilter` option, they reduced HAR files to API calls only (average 800 KB) — a 98% reduction that brought artifact storage costs from $85/month to $2/month for a 200-test suite.

```typescript
// tests/network-capture.spec.ts — HAR tracing with urlFilter
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

test('checkout flow network traffic', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();

  // Start HAR recording — filter to API calls only to control file size.
  // await using ensures stopHar() is called even on test failure.
  await using _har = {
    [Symbol.asyncDispose]: async () => {
      await context.tracing.stopHar();
      await context.close();
    },
  };

  await context.tracing.startHar(
    path.join('test-results', `checkout-${Date.now()}.har`),
    {
      // Only capture API calls — skip static assets, fonts, images
      urlFilter: '**/api/**',
    }
  );

  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();

  // Assert network traffic patterns
  // (HAR file available for inspection after test completes)
  await expect(page.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible();
});
```

### Sentinel Job Pattern for Stable Required Status Checks

When a CI pipeline uses dynamic matrix generation (shard count varies based on changed files), job names like `e2e (1)`, `e2e (2)` are unstable — they change when the shard count changes. Branch protection required status checks match job names exactly, so a shard count change breaks the check configuration. The sentinel job pattern decouples the required check name from the matrix by introducing a terminal job with a stable name that depends on all matrix jobs.

This pattern also solves the "empty matrix" problem: when no test files changed (documentation-only PRs), the matrix produces zero jobs, and normally the required check is never reported. The sentinel job runs unconditionally and fast-passes when its dependencies are all skipped.

> [community] An 8-engineer team used dynamic sharding with a 1-to-8 shard range. After a sprint that added many new test files, the dynamic shard count jumped from 4 to 6. All PRs that week failed to merge because the required check `e2e (5)` and `e2e (6)` had never been registered in branch protection. The sentinel pattern (`e2e-complete: needs: [e2e]`) was added retroactively — it required updating branch protection rules only once, to replace `e2e (1)` through `e2e (4)` with the single `e2e-complete` entry.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e-sentinel.yml — stable required status check via sentinel
name: E2E

on: [pull_request, merge_group]

jobs:
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.compute.outputs.matrix }}
      shard-total: ${{ steps.compute.outputs.shardTotal }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Compute shards
        id: compute
        run: npx tsx scripts/compute-shard-matrix.ts
        env:
          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}

  e2e:
    needs: setup
    if: needs.setup.outputs.matrix != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shardIndex: ${{ fromJson(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --shard=${{ matrix.shardIndex }}/${{ needs.setup.outputs.shard-total }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: blob-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
          path: blob-report/
          retention-days: 1

  # SENTINEL JOB — register this job name in branch protection required checks.
  # Name never changes regardless of shard count or empty matrix.
  # Always runs; fast-passes on documentation-only PRs (skipped e2e jobs).
  e2e-complete:
    if: always()
    needs: [setup, e2e]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check e2e result
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ needs.e2e.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then
            echo "E2E tests failed"
            exit 1
          elif [[ "${{ needs.e2e.result }}" == "skipped" ||
                  "${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}" == "[]" ]]; then
            echo "No e2e tests to run (documentation-only PR or empty matrix)"
            exit 0
          else
            echo "E2E tests passed (${{ needs.setup.outputs.shard-total }} shards)"
            exit 0
          fi
```

## New Anti-Patterns (Cycle 23)

| Anti-pattern | Why harmful | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Using `test.skip()` in fixtures for missing CI credentials | Produces green CI runs with 0 tests executed — required status checks pass on empty suites | Use `test.abort(message)` (Playwright v1.60+) which exits with code 1, failing the status check and surfacing the misconfiguration |
| `coverage.changed: process.env['GITHUB_BASE_REF']` without event-type guard | On `push` to main and `merge_group` events, `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is empty — the option computes diff against an empty base, reporting 100% coverage on zero files | Guard the option: `changed: process.env['GITHUB_BASE_REF'] || false`; always run full coverage on main and merge queue events |
| Per-repository IAM allow-lists for OIDC CI credentials | Maintenance burden scales O(N repositories); outdated policies create orphaned access or block new repos | Switch to `repo_property_*` attribute-based trust policies (GA March 2025); grant access by repository property, not by enumerated name |
| Docker `COPY . .` before `npm ci` in Dockerfile.test | Source code changes (every commit) invalidate the `npm ci` layer — `node_modules` re-downloaded on every build despite no dependency changes | Split into two `COPY` instructions: `COPY package*.json ./` before `RUN npm ci`, then `COPY . .` after — dependency layer only rebuilds when `package.json` changes |
| `jest.spyOn()` without `afterEach(() => jest.restoreAllMocks())` | Spy implementations persist across tests in the same worker — causes order-dependent failures in CI where tests run in a different sequence than locally | Use Jest 30's `using` keyword: `using spy = jest.spyOn(...)` auto-restores on block exit; or add `restoreMocks: true` to jest config |
| Vitest `--detect-async-leaks` in all environments | The 5–10% overhead per test file adds meaningful latency to fast unit suites run hundreds of times per day locally | Enable only in CI: `detectAsyncLeaks: process.env['CI'] === 'true'`; run locally only as an audit pass when diagnosing flakiness |

## New Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 23)

**#76** [community] Jest 30's `globalsCleanup: 'on'` cleans up properties added to `globalThis` between test files — but only for properties that were **not present** when the test environment was initialized. Properties set by `setupFilesAfterFramework` are considered "initial state" and are not cleaned up. If a test adds new properties to `globalThis` (e.g., `globalThis.myTestHelper = ...`), those are cleaned; if `setupFilesAfterEnach` sets `globalThis.myTestHelper`, it persists across files. Use `protectProperties(globalThis.myTestHelper)` explicitly to document the intentional persistence rather than relying on implicit initialization order.

**#77** [community] Playwright `tracing.startHar()` with `content: 'embed'` buffers all response bodies in memory before writing to disk. For API-heavy test flows that stream large JSON payloads (pagination endpoints returning 10,000 items), this can exhaust runner memory. Use `content: 'omit'` for HAR recordings used only for replay (body not needed for URL/timing analysis) or `urlFilter` to restrict recording to specific API paths. The default is `content: 'attach'` (save body to separate files alongside the HAR) which is safer for CI.

**#78** [community] GitHub OIDC `repo_property_*` claims are only included in tokens issued for **workflow runs**, not for matrix job tokens or composite action contexts. Teams that define the trust condition on `repo_property_team` find that sub-jobs in a matrix with different `permissions:` blocks do not inherit the property claim. The fix: ensure the job that calls `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` has `permissions: id-token: write` defined at the job level, not inherited from the workflow level, and that the OIDC token is requested from the job context (not a composite action with its own `permissions`).

**#79** [community] Docker BuildKit's `type=gha` cache backend has a per-scope size limit (default: 10 GB for GitHub-hosted runners). In monorepos with multiple services, each service typically defines its own `scope` for isolation — but total cache consumption across all scopes counts toward the 10 GB limit. Teams building 6+ Docker images per PR run find that older scopes are evicted (cache miss) even though the individual scope is under 2 GB. Fix: prefix scopes with a date-based eviction key (`scope=service-a-${{ github.run_id }}`) for ephemeral images, and use persistent scopes only for stable base layers.

**#80** [community] Vitest `aroundEach` and `aroundAll` hooks (v4.1+) execute in the order they are **registered**, not in test-nesting order. A top-level `aroundAll` that starts a database container registers first; a nested `describe` block that registers its own `aroundAll` for schema migration registers second. They run in registration order, so the schema migration runs inside the container start (correct). However, if a developer adds a third `aroundAll` in a new `describe` block at the top level (after the nested block), it runs after the nested block's `aroundAll` — even though it appears visually "above" the nested block in file order. Registration order equals declaration order within a file; across files, it follows test file execution order.

**#81** [community] Jest 30 `expect.arrayOf` does not work as an asymmetric matcher inside `toHaveBeenCalledWith`. Calling `expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.arrayOf(...))` throws a `TypeError: expect.arrayOf is not a function` because `expect.arrayOf` is only available as a top-level assertion (`.toEqual`, `.toMatchObject`), not as a nested asymmetric matcher in `toHaveBeenCalledWith`. Use `expect.arrayContaining([expect.objectContaining(...)])` as the equivalent inside `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.

**#82** [community] SLSA provenance generation with `actions/attest-build-provenance` requires the workflow to run on a GitHub-hosted runner (not self-hosted) for Sigstore signing to succeed. Teams using self-hosted runners for cost reasons find the attestation step fails with `SLSA provenance signing requires a GitHub-hosted runner`. The workaround is a two-job workflow: run tests on the self-hosted runner, then pass the artifact to a GitHub-hosted runner job for provenance generation. This adds ~30 seconds but preserves cost savings for the test execution phase.

### Pattern 1 — Vitest Shard + Blob Reporter: File-Level Distribution with Merged Coverage

Vitest splits test **files** across shards, not individual test cases. A suite of 1,000 files with `--shard=1/4` runs exactly 250 files per shard regardless of individual test case counts. The `blob` reporter writes raw binary output per shard; the `--merge-reports` command combines all blobs into a single HTML/JSON/lcov report including merged coverage. This split means coverage data must also be merged — a step teams commonly omit, producing incomplete coverage artifacts from only the last shard's report file.

The correct three-phase pattern: (1) run shards with `--reporter=blob --coverage`, (2) upload `.vitest-reports/` artifacts per shard, (3) run a merge job that downloads all shard artifacts and executes `vitest --merge-reports=.vitest-reports --coverage --reporter=lcov`.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/vitest-sharded.yml
name: Vitest Sharded

on: [pull_request, push]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Run shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4
        run: |
          npx vitest run \
            --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4 \
            --reporter=blob \
            --coverage \
            --coverage.reporter=json
        env:
          CI: 'true'
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: vitest-blob-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: .vitest-reports/
          retention-days: 1

  merge-reports:
    if: always()
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: vitest-blob-*
          path: .vitest-reports/
          merge-multiple: true
      # Merge all shard blobs → single HTML report + merged lcov coverage
      - name: Merge reports
        run: |
          npx vitest --merge-reports=.vitest-reports \
            --reporter=html \
            --reporter=github-actions \
            --coverage \
            --coverage.reporter=lcov \
            --coverage.reporter=text-summary
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: vitest-html-report
          path: html/
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coverage-lcov
          path: coverage/lcov.info
```

**Tradeoff:** Vitest shards by file count, not by execution time. A shard containing 50 slow integration test files takes much longer than one with 50 fast unit test files. For uneven suites, pair with a test-timing-aware shard matrix script (similar to the Playwright `compute-shard-matrix.ts` pattern from Cycle 23) that groups files by their historical run time rather than by simple numeric division.

### Pattern 2 — Vitest Workspace Project Filtering in CI

Vitest workspace mode lets a monorepo define multiple test projects with different environments (browser, jsdom, node) in a single `vitest.workspace.ts`. Each project can set its own `include` patterns, `environment`, and `pool`. In CI, the `--project` CLI flag filters to specific projects — enabling targeted pipelines that run only the affected workspace project without spinning up all environments.

```typescript
// vitest.workspace.ts — monorepo multi-environment workspace
import { defineWorkspace } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineWorkspace([
  {
    // Node.js unit tests — fastest, run on every commit
    test: {
      name: 'unit',
      include: ['packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts'],
      environment: 'node',
      pool: 'threads',
    },
  },
  {
    // Browser component tests — run only on UI package changes
    test: {
      name: 'browser',
      include: ['packages/ui/**/*.test.tsx'],
      browser: {
        enabled: true,
        provider: 'playwright',
        name: 'chromium',
      },
    },
  },
  {
    // Integration tests — run in node with longer timeout
    test: {
      name: 'integration',
      include: ['packages/*/src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
      environment: 'node',
      pool: 'forks', // forks > threads for tests that spawn child processes
      testTimeout: 30_000,
      hookTimeout: 30_000,
    },
  },
]);
```

```yaml
# CI pipeline — project-filtered jobs in GitHub Actions
jobs:
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --project=unit

  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: unit  # only run if unit passes (fail-fast ordering)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --project=integration
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.CI_DATABASE_URL }}
```

**Note:** The `extends: true` option in project configuration causes a project to inherit all root-level config settings. Without it, project configs are completely standalone — root-level `globalSetup`, `reporters`, and `coverage` are not inherited. A common mistake is assuming root-level reporters apply to project runs; they do not unless `extends: true` is set.

---

### Pattern 3 — Docker `RUN --mount=type=cache` for Dependency Layers in Test Images

Docker BuildKit cache mounts (`RUN --mount=type=cache`) persist the package manager cache directory between builds **without adding the cache to the image layer**. Unlike `COPY package.json && RUN npm ci` (which requires the package.json layer to be intact), cache mounts work even when `package.json` changes — the mount reuses already-downloaded `.npm` cache entries for unchanged packages, downloading only the delta. This is substantially faster than no caching for medium-to-large dependency graphs.

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile.test — BuildKit cache mounts for CI test images
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.9
FROM node:22-slim AS base
WORKDIR /app

# --- dependency layer (cached by package-lock.json hash) ---
# RUN --mount=type=cache persists ~/.npm between builds.
# The cache key is per-image by default; use --mount=type=cache,id=npm
# to share the npm cache across multiple images in a monorepo.
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm,id=npm \
    npm ci --prefer-offline

# --- source layer (invalidated on every commit) ---
COPY . .

# --- test stage ---
FROM base AS test
CMD ["npx", "vitest", "run", "--reporter=verbose"]
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docker-test.yml — BuildKit GHA cache backend
name: Docker Tests

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  docker-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
        # BuildKit is required for --mount=type=cache and type=gha backend

      - name: Build test image (with GHA cache)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile.test
          target: test
          load: true
          tags: myapp-test:pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          # GHA cache backend: stores layers in GitHub Actions cache storage
          # scope isolates per-Dockerfile to avoid cross-image eviction
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=test-image
          cache-to: type=gha,scope=test-image,mode=max

      - name: Run tests in container
        run: docker run --rm myapp-test:pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
```

**Tradeoff:** `type=gha` cache scope shares the 10 GB GitHub Actions cache budget with `actions/cache` steps. Monorepos building multiple Docker images should use a stable scope per image (`scope=test-image-$SERVICE`) but monitor total cache usage. When total cache exceeds 10 GB, GitHub evicts the oldest scopes first — which may be the base image cache, not ephemeral application images.

### Pattern 4 — SLSA Level 2 Provenance via Two-Job Workflow

SLSA (Supply chain Levels for Software Artifacts) Level 2 requires that build provenance is generated by the build platform itself (not by the build script) and is signed with a service account controlled by the platform. GitHub Actions achieves this via `actions/attest-build-provenance`, which calls the Sigstore Fulcio CA using the workflow's OIDC token to produce a signed attestation. The attestation is stored in GitHub's immutable attestation registry and can be verified offline with `gh attestation verify`.

The critical constraint: Sigstore signing requires a GitHub-hosted runner. Teams on self-hosted runners must split test execution from attestation into two jobs.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/release.yml — SLSA Level 2 provenance with two-job split
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

jobs:
  # Job 1: Build and test on self-hosted runner (cost-efficient)
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    outputs:
      artifact-digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

      - name: Build distribution artifact
        id: build
        run: |
          npm run build
          # Compute SHA-256 digest for the artifact
          DIGEST=$(sha256sum dist/app.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)
          echo "digest=sha256:$DIGEST" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-artifact
          path: dist/app.tar.gz

  # Job 2: Attest on GitHub-hosted runner (required for Sigstore signing)
  attest:
    needs: build-and-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest  # MUST be GitHub-hosted for Sigstore OIDC
    permissions:
      id-token: write    # Required for OIDC Sigstore signing
      attestations: write # Required to write to attestation registry
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-artifact
          path: dist/

      - name: Generate SLSA provenance attestation
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
        with:
          subject-path: dist/app.tar.gz
          # Attestation is stored in GitHub's immutable registry.
          # Verify with: gh attestation verify dist/app.tar.gz --repo owner/repo
```

**Verify locally:**
```bash
gh attestation verify dist/app.tar.gz --repo my-org/my-repo
# Output: Attestation verified. SLSA Level 2 provenance confirmed.
```

### Pattern 5 — GitLab CI `parallel:matrix` for Test Distribution

GitLab CI's `parallel:matrix` keyword creates independent jobs for every combination of matrix variables, each running the same script with different environment variables. Unlike GitHub Actions `strategy.matrix`, GitLab's implementation does not require a separate setup job for dynamic matrix computation — the matrix is declared inline in the job YAML. For test sharding, set `SHARD_INDEX` and `SHARD_TOTAL` as matrix variables and reference them in the test command.

```yaml
# .gitlab-ci.yml — parallel:matrix test sharding
stages:
  - test
  - report

unit-tests:
  stage: test
  image: node:22-slim
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - package-lock.json
    paths:
      - node_modules/
  script:
    - npm ci --prefer-offline
    - npx vitest run
        --shard=$SHARD_INDEX/$SHARD_TOTAL
        --reporter=blob
        --reporter=junit
        --outputFile.junit=reports/junit-$SHARD_INDEX.xml
  parallel:
    matrix:
      - SHARD_INDEX: [1, 2, 3, 4]
        SHARD_TOTAL: [4]
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      # GitLab parses JUnit XML and renders test results in the MR widget
      junit: reports/junit-*.xml
    paths:
      - .vitest-reports/
    expire_in: 1 day

merge-reports:
  stage: report
  image: node:22-slim
  needs:
    - unit-tests
  script:
    - npm ci --prefer-offline
    - npx vitest --merge-reports=.vitest-reports --reporter=html
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - html/
    expire_in: 7 days
```

**Key difference from GitHub Actions:** GitLab's `artifacts.reports.junit` keyword is parsed by GitLab and displayed in the Merge Request widget as a test summary with pass/fail counts, new failures, and fixed failures. This requires JUnit XML format (not JSON or TAP). Teams running Playwright in GitLab should use `--reporter=junit` alongside `--reporter=blob` for shard runs.

---

### Pattern 6 — Node.js 24 Built-in Test Runner with `--experimental-test-coverage`

Node.js 22+ ships a built-in test runner (`node:test`) that supports concurrent tests, `describe`/`it`, mocking, and coverage reporting without any additional dependencies. Node.js 24 (released April 2025) promotes `--experimental-test-coverage` to stable and adds `--test-global-setup` for one-time setup across test files. For teams that want zero-dependency testing for utility libraries or internal tools, the built-in runner eliminates the Jest/Vitest dependency entirely.

```typescript
// src/utils/math.test.ts — Node.js 24 built-in test runner
import { describe, it, beforeEach } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { add, divide } from './math.js';

describe('math utilities', () => {
  describe('add()', () => {
    it('returns the sum of two numbers', () => {
      assert.equal(add(2, 3), 5);
    });

    it('handles negative numbers', () => {
      assert.equal(add(-1, 1), 0);
    });
  });

  describe('divide()', () => {
    it('returns the quotient', () => {
      assert.equal(divide(10, 2), 5);
    });

    it('throws on division by zero', () => {
      assert.throws(() => divide(10, 0), { message: 'Division by zero' });
    });
  });
});
```

```bash
# Run with coverage (stable in Node.js 24)
node --test --experimental-test-coverage \
  --test-reporter=spec \
  --test-reporter-destination=stdout \
  'src/**/*.test.ts'
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/node-test.yml — Node.js 24 built-in test runner
name: Node.js Tests

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Run tests with coverage
        run: |
          node --test \
            --experimental-test-coverage \
            --test-reporter=tap \
            --test-reporter-destination=stdout \
            'src/**/*.test.ts'
```

**Tradeoff:** The built-in runner's mocking API (`mock.fn()`, `mock.method()`, `mock.module()`) is less ergonomic than Jest/Vitest. Module mocking (`mock.module()`) requires `--experimental-vm-modules` and does not support TypeScript transforms via `tsx` or `ts-node` — teams must transpile to JS first or use `--import tsx/esm` with caveats. For codebases with extensive mocking, Jest or Vitest remains the better choice. The built-in runner shines for pure-Node utility libraries with minimal mocking needs.

---

### Pattern 7 — Turborepo Remote Cache for Test Results

Turborepo's remote cache treats test runs as tasks with deterministic inputs and outputs. When no test input files have changed (source files, test files, config, env hash), Turborepo replays the cached test run result — printing previous output and exiting with the same code — without actually running tests. In a large monorepo with 50 packages, this can reduce CI test execution from 15 minutes to under 30 seconds for PRs that touch only a single package.

```json
// turbo.json — test task with cache fingerprint configuration
{
  "$schema": "https://turborepo.com/schema.json",
  "tasks": {
    "test": {
      "dependsOn": ["^build"],
      "inputs": [
        "src/**/*.ts",
        "src/**/*.tsx",
        "test/**/*.ts",
        "vitest.config.ts",
        "tsconfig.json",
        "package.json"
      ],
      "outputs": [
        "coverage/**",
        ".vitest-reports/**"
      ],
      "cache": true,
      "env": [
        "NODE_ENV",
        "CI"
      ]
    },
    "test:e2e": {
      "dependsOn": ["^build"],
      "inputs": ["e2e/**/*.ts", "playwright.config.ts"],
      "outputs": ["playwright-report/**", "test-results/**"],
      "cache": false  // E2E tests must always run — external state not fingerprinted
    }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — Turborepo remote cache with Vercel
name: CI

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Run tests (cached)
        run: npx turbo run test --filter=...[origin/main]
        env:
          TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
          TURBO_TEAM: ${{ vars.TURBO_TEAM }}
          # --filter=...[origin/main] runs only packages changed vs main
```

**Anti-pattern — caching E2E tests:** E2E tests interact with external state (databases, APIs, deployed services). Their "pass" result depends on the state of the system under test, not just the test code. Setting `cache: true` for E2E tasks means a previously-passing run is replayed as a cache hit even when the deployed application has changed. Always set `cache: false` for E2E tasks and any test that touches live infrastructure.

---

### Pattern 8 — Testcontainers Lifecycle Management for Integration Test Isolation

`testcontainers-node` starts Docker containers programmatically within test setup, ensuring each test run (or test file) gets a clean, isolated database or service instance. The Ryuk container reaper cleans up containers even when the test process crashes — preventing container accumulation on shared CI runners. The key pattern is using `GenericContainer` with a health check wait strategy rather than a fixed-duration sleep, and sharing a single container instance across a test file via `beforeAll`/`afterAll`.

```typescript
// tests/setup/postgres.ts — testcontainers integration for CI
import { GenericContainer, Wait, type StartedTestContainer } from 'testcontainers';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

let container: StartedTestContainer;
let pool: Pool;

export async function startPostgres(): Promise<Pool> {
  container = await new GenericContainer('postgres:16-alpine')
    .withEnvironment({
      POSTGRES_USER: 'test',
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 'test',
      POSTGRES_DB: 'testdb',
    })
    // Wait for TCP port before returning — no sleep() needed
    .withWaitStrategy(Wait.forHealthCheck())
    .withHealthCheck({
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U test'],
      interval: 1_000,
      timeout: 3_000,
      retries: 5,
    })
    // Expose random host port to avoid conflicts on parallel CI workers
    .withExposedPorts(5432)
    .start();

  const mappedPort = container.getMappedPort(5432);
  pool = new Pool({
    host: container.getHost(),
    port: mappedPort,
    user: 'test',
    password: 'test',
    database: 'testdb',
  });

  return pool;
}

export async function stopPostgres(): Promise<void> {
  await pool?.end();
  await container?.stop();
}
```

```typescript
// tests/user-repository.test.ts — testcontainers lifecycle in Vitest
import { describe, it, beforeAll, afterAll, expect } from 'vitest';
import { startPostgres, stopPostgres } from './setup/postgres.js';
import { UserRepository } from '../src/user-repository.js';
import type { Pool } from 'pg';

let pool: Pool;
let repo: UserRepository;

beforeAll(async () => {
  pool = await startPostgres();
  // Run migrations against the fresh container
  await pool.query(`
    CREATE TABLE users (
      id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
      email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
    )
  `);
  repo = new UserRepository(pool);
}, 60_000); // allow 60s for container startup on slow CI runners

afterAll(async () => {
  await stopPostgres();
});

describe('UserRepository', () => {
  it('creates and retrieves a user', async () => {
    const user = await repo.create({ email: 'test@example.com' });
    const found = await repo.findById(user.id);
    expect(found?.email).toBe('test@example.com');
  });
});
```

**CI consideration:** Testcontainers requires a Docker socket accessible to the test runner. GitHub Actions' `ubuntu-latest` runners have Docker available by default. For self-hosted runners without Docker, use `TESTCONTAINERS_HOST_OVERRIDE` and `DOCKER_HOST` env vars to point to a remote Docker daemon. Set `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` only as a last resort — Ryuk prevents container accumulation after OOM-killed processes.

---

### Pattern 9 — Playwright Worker-Index Database Isolation for Parallel Tests

When Playwright runs tests in parallel across multiple workers, integration tests that touch a real database create race conditions: worker 1 creates a user with `email=test@example.com` while worker 2 also tries to create the same user. The solution is worker-index-based database namespace isolation: each worker uses a separate schema, database name suffix, or seeded tenant ID derived from `process.env.TEST_WORKER_INDEX`.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — worker-index database isolation
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  globalSetup: './tests/global-setup.ts',
  workers: 4,
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',
  },
  projects: [
    { name: 'chromium', use: { browserName: 'chromium' } },
  ],
});
```

```typescript
// tests/global-setup.ts — provision one DB schema per worker
import { chromium, type FullConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

export default async function globalSetup(config: FullConfig): Promise<void> {
  const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env['DATABASE_URL'] });

  // Create isolated schema for each worker (0-indexed)
  const workerCount = config.workers ?? 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < workerCount; i++) {
    await pool.query(`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS test_worker_${i}`);
    await pool.query(`SET search_path TO test_worker_${i}`);
    // Run migrations for this schema...
  }

  await pool.end();
}
```

```typescript
// tests/fixtures.ts — per-worker database connection in fixtures
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

type WorkerFixtures = {
  db: Pool;
  workerSchema: string;
};

export const test = base.extend<{}, WorkerFixtures>({
  // Worker-scoped fixture: initialized once per worker, not per test
  workerSchema: [
    async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
      const schema = `test_worker_${workerInfo.workerIndex}`;
      await use(schema);
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],

  db: [
    async ({ workerSchema }, use) => {
      const pool = new Pool({
        connectionString: process.env['DATABASE_URL'],
        // All queries in this worker run in the worker's schema
        options: `-c search_path=${workerSchema}`,
      });
      await use(pool);
      await pool.end();
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

export { expect };
```

---

### Pattern 10 — GitHub Actions `concurrency` Group for PR Pipeline Deduplication

Without concurrency controls, every push to a feature branch triggers a new workflow run while the previous run is still executing. In active development with rapid pushes, this wastes 3–5× the runner minutes and creates confusing results where an older run's failure email arrives after the newer run has already succeeded. GitHub Actions `concurrency` groups cancel in-progress runs for the same branch when a new push arrives, ensuring only the latest commit's pipeline produces a result.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — concurrency group pattern
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch on new push.
# group: unique per PR number (for PRs) or per branch (for pushes to main).
# cancel-in-progress: only cancel on feature branches; never cancel on main.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
```

**Warning:** `cancel-in-progress: true` globally cancels all jobs, including deploy jobs. For workflows that contain both test and deploy stages, scope the concurrency to the test job or use separate workflows — one for tests (cancellable) and one for deployments (never cancellable). Cancelling a deploy job mid-execution can leave infrastructure in a partially-migrated state.

---

### Pattern 11 — Merge Queue (`merge_group`) Event Guard for Required Checks

GitHub's merge queue groups PRs into batches and validates the merged result before adding to the main branch. Workflows must explicitly handle the `merge_group` event to run during queue processing. Status checks registered for merge queue must pass before the PR lands. A common failure mode: the CI workflow runs on `pull_request` but not on `merge_group`, so the merge queue runs with no status checks — allowing broken commits to merge if all PRs passed individually but fail when combined.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — merge_group event handling
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  merge_group:
    # Run the same checks for merge queue batches as for individual PRs
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

  # Sentinel job: stable name for branch protection required check.
  # Register THIS job name in branch protection, not the dynamic matrix jobs.
  ci-complete:
    if: always()
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check CI result
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ needs.test.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CI passed"
```

**ISTQB alignment:** The merge queue corresponds to the "test level" boundary between developer-side testing (unit, integration, component) and system-level verification (full build + combined PR batches). It enforces that the "test object" (the merged branch tip) satisfies all required test conditions before modifying the protected branch.

---

### Pattern 12 — Fail-Fast Ordering with Explicit `needs` Dependency Chain

The ISTQB principle of test ordering maps to CI pipeline stage dependencies. Fast, cheap test levels (unit) should run before slow, expensive ones (E2E). In GitHub Actions, this is implemented with `needs:` dependency chains — each stage explicitly waiting for the previous. Without explicit `needs`, all jobs run in parallel regardless of logical ordering, wasting minutes running E2E setup while trivial unit tests would have caught the failure in 30 seconds.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/full-pipeline.yml — fail-fast ordering with needs chains
name: Full Pipeline

on: [pull_request, merge_group]

jobs:
  # Level 1: Unit tests — fastest, highest confidence signal (~1 min)
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --project=unit

  # Level 2: Integration tests — requires unit to pass (~3 min)
  integration:
    needs: unit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx vitest run --project=integration

  # Level 3: E2E tests — requires integration to pass (~10 min)
  e2e:
    needs: integration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npx playwright test

  # Sentinel for branch protection
  pipeline-complete:
    if: always()
    needs: [unit, integration, e2e]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Evaluate pipeline result
        run: |
          RESULTS=("${{ needs.unit.result }}" "${{ needs.integration.result }}" "${{ needs.e2e.result }}")
          for r in "${RESULTS[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$r" == "failure" ]]; then
              echo "Pipeline failed"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "Pipeline passed"
```

---

### Pattern 13 — Environment Parity: Container-Based Staging Environments

Martin Fowler's Continuous Integration article states: "Use the same database software, with the same versions, use the same version of the operating system." In modern practice, this is achieved with Docker Compose files that mirror production topology: same database version, same Redis version, same message broker. The staging environment is defined as `docker-compose.staging.yml` and is used identically in both CI pipelines and developer-local pre-production checks.

```yaml
# docker-compose.staging.yml — production-mirrored staging environment
version: '3.9'

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      target: production
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: staging
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app:secret@postgres:5432/appdb
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.3-alpine  # Pin to exact patch version — same as production
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
      POSTGRES_DB: appdb
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'pg_isready', '-U', 'app']
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2.4-alpine  # Pin to exact patch version — same as production
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/staging-e2e.yml — staging environment in CI
name: Staging E2E

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  staging-e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Start staging environment
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d --wait
        # --wait waits for all healthchecks to pass before continuing

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run E2E against staging
        run: npx playwright test
        env:
          BASE_URL: http://localhost:3000

      - name: Collect logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml logs

      - name: Stop staging environment
        if: always()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml down -v
```

**Anti-pattern — using `latest` tags:** `postgres:latest` and `redis:latest` resolve to different minor versions over time. A CI run that passes today may fail next month when `latest` resolves to Postgres 17 and your app uses a Postgres 16-only feature. Always pin to exact patch versions for external dependencies in test environments.

---

### Pattern 14 — OpenTelemetry Trace-Based Test Observability

OpenTelemetry (OTel) trace spans emitted during test execution give CI pipelines observability into test behavior beyond pass/fail. Each test suite emits a root span; assertions, database calls, and HTTP requests inside tests emit child spans. The trace shows exactly which database query caused a slow test, what HTTP calls were made to mock servers, and whether retry logic was triggered. This pattern is particularly valuable for diagnosing flakiness: the trace shows that a test passed after 2 retries because the first attempt hit a TCP timeout on a Redis connection.

```typescript
// tests/otel-setup.ts — OpenTelemetry trace setup for CI test runs
import { NodeSDK } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-node';
import { OTLPTraceExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http';
import { Resource } from '@opentelemetry/resources';
import { SemanticResourceAttributes } from '@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions';
import { BatchSpanProcessor } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base';

// Only enable in CI — local dev does not need trace overhead
if (process.env['CI']) {
  const sdk = new NodeSDK({
    resource: new Resource({
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME]: 'test-suite',
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_VERSION]: process.env['GITHUB_SHA'] ?? 'local',
      'ci.workflow': process.env['GITHUB_WORKFLOW'] ?? 'unknown',
      'ci.run_id': process.env['GITHUB_RUN_ID'] ?? 'unknown',
    }),
    spanProcessors: [
      new BatchSpanProcessor(
        new OTLPTraceExporter({
          url: process.env['OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT'] ?? 'http://localhost:4318/v1/traces',
        }),
      ),
    ],
  });

  sdk.start();

  // Flush traces before process exit (important for short-lived test processes)
  process.on('beforeExit', async () => {
    await sdk.shutdown();
  });
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-with-otel.yml — CI with OTel trace collection
name: CI with Traces

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      # Lightweight OTel collector sidecar
      otel-collector:
        image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.100.0
        ports:
          - 4318:4318  # OTLP HTTP
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Run tests with tracing
        run: npx vitest run
        env:
          CI: 'true'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://localhost:4318
```

---

### Pattern 15 — Flaky Test Quarantine with `--repeat-each` and Reporting Gate

Flaky tests — those that pass on some runs and fail on others without code changes — undermine CI trust. The correct strategy is not to delete or permanently skip them, but to quarantine them: tag them, continue running them separately, and report flakiness metrics without blocking the pipeline. The `--repeat-each=3` flag (Playwright) and `test.extend` with retry-aware fixture (Vitest) allow running suspected flaky tests 3× to measure actual failure rate. A separate "flakiness report" job runs these tests without blocking the main pipeline's required status check.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/flaky-audit.yml — flaky test quarantine audit
name: Flaky Test Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * *'  # Run nightly, not on every PR
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  flaky-audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run quarantined tests 3× to measure flakiness rate
        # --grep matches tests tagged @flaky in their title
        # --repeat-each=3 runs each matched test 3 times
        # --reporter=json captures results for analysis
        run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --grep="@flaky" \
            --repeat-each=3 \
            --reporter=json \
            --output=flaky-results.json || true  # Don't fail the job
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Parse flakiness report
        run: |
          node -e "
            const r = require('./flaky-results.json');
            const tests = r.suites.flatMap(s => s.specs);
            const stats = tests.map(t => ({
              title: t.title,
              passed: t.tests.filter(r => r.status === 'passed').length,
              failed: t.tests.filter(r => r.status === 'failed').length,
              flakeRate: t.tests.filter(r => r.status === 'failed').length / t.tests.length,
            }));
            console.table(stats.filter(s => s.flakeRate > 0).sort((a,b) => b.flakeRate - a.flakeRate));
          "

      - name: Post summary to GitHub Step Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "## Flaky Test Audit — $(date '+%Y-%m-%d')" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "See artifacts for full JSON report" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: flaky-audit-results
          path: flaky-results.json
```

```typescript
// Tagging a test for quarantine — Playwright
// Mark with @flaky in title — grep pattern picks it up in audit workflow
test('@flaky - payment webhook arrives within 5s', async ({ page }) => {
  // This test is timing-sensitive and flaky ~15% of runs.
  // It is excluded from the main pipeline via --grep-invert="@flaky"
  // and only runs in the nightly flaky-audit.yml workflow.
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.click('[data-testid="pay-button"]');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="success-banner"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
});
```

### Pattern 16 — Container Structure Test for Image Validation in CI

`container-structure-test` (Google) validates that a Docker image has the correct structure: specific files exist at expected paths, commands produce expected output, and environment variables are set. For test pipeline images, this verifies that the test runner binary exists, the correct Node.js version is installed, and test fixtures are present before committing to a full test run. This is particularly valuable for teams that build custom test runner images for use across multiple repositories.

```yaml
# container-structure-test.yaml — validates the test runner image
schemaVersion: '2.0.0'

commandTests:
  - name: 'node version is 22.x'
    command: 'node'
    args: ['--version']
    expectedOutput:
      - '^v22\.'

  - name: 'npx is available'
    command: 'npx'
    args: ['--version']
    expectedOutput:
      - '^10\.'

  - name: 'playwright is installed'
    command: 'npx'
    args: ['playwright', '--version']
    expectedOutput:
      - 'Version 1\.'

fileExistenceTests:
  - name: 'playwright.config.ts exists'
    path: '/app/playwright.config.ts'
    shouldExist: true

  - name: 'node_modules are installed'
    path: '/app/node_modules'
    shouldExist: true

  - name: 'Chromium binary is present'
    path: '/root/.cache/ms-playwright'
    shouldExist: true

environmentTests:
  - name: 'NODE_ENV is set'
    envVars:
      NODE_ENV: 'test'
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/test-image.yml — image validation in CI
name: Validate Test Image

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'Dockerfile.test'
      - 'package-lock.json'
      - '.github/workflows/test-image.yml'

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build test image
        run: docker build -f Dockerfile.test -t myapp-test:local .

      - name: Install container-structure-test
        run: |
          curl -LO https://storage.googleapis.com/container-structure-test/latest/container-structure-test-linux-amd64
          chmod +x container-structure-test-linux-amd64
          sudo mv container-structure-test-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/container-structure-test

      - name: Validate image structure
        run: |
          container-structure-test test \
            --image myapp-test:local \
            --config container-structure-test.yaml
```

## New Anti-Patterns (Cycle 24)

| Anti-pattern | Why harmful | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Vitest shard runs with `--coverage` but no `--merge-reports` job | Each shard writes its own coverage JSON to `coverage/` — the last artifact uploaded overwrites previous ones, producing coverage data from only N/4 of test files | Add a `merge-reports` job that downloads all shard artifacts and runs `vitest --merge-reports --coverage` to produce accurate merged coverage |
| Turborepo `cache: true` for E2E tasks | Caches the "pass" result against test-file hash, not application state — a cached pass is replayed even when the deployed app changes | Set `cache: false` for all tasks that interact with live infrastructure or deployed services |
| `docker-compose up` without `--wait` in CI | Container starts but service not yet healthy — test runner connects before database accepts queries, producing intermittent connection refused failures | Use `docker compose up -d --wait` (Compose v2.x) which respects healthchecks and only returns after all services report healthy |
| Missing `merge_group` event in CI workflow triggers | Merge queue runs with no status checks — the queue processes batches without any test gate, allowing integration failures to reach main | Add `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]` to workflow `on:` triggers and register a stable sentinel job as the required check |
| Concurrency `cancel-in-progress: true` on workflows with deploy jobs | Cancels an in-progress deploy mid-execution, leaving infrastructure in a partially-applied state (e.g., schema migration started but not completed) | Use separate workflows for tests (cancellable) and deployments (never cancellable); or scope the concurrency group to test jobs only |
| Hardcoded `SHARD_TOTAL` as a magic number in CI matrix | Changing shard count requires editing the matrix in multiple places; mismatches produce incorrect coverage | Define shard total as a single workflow-level env var or job output referenced by all matrix entries |

---

## New Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 24)

**#83** [community] Vitest `--merge-reports` silently ignores shard blob files that were generated with a different Vitest version. When a monorepo has multiple packages each with their own `vitest` version pinned in `package.json`, shard blobs from package A (Vitest 3.x) and package B (Vitest 4.x) cannot be merged in the same `--merge-reports` invocation. The merge command exits with code 0 but produces a report covering only the blobs from the matching version. Ensure all packages use the same Vitest version and declare it as a workspace root `devDependency`.

**#84** [community] Docker Compose `--wait` in CI only waits for services with a `healthcheck` defined. Services without a healthcheck are considered "ready" immediately after container start, regardless of whether the process inside is actually accepting connections. Teams that add a new service to `docker-compose.staging.yml` without a healthcheck find that tests start before the service is ready — causing intermittent connection failures that appear random. Every service in a test compose file must have a healthcheck; add a lint step that fails if any service lacks one.

**#85** [community] GitHub Actions `actions/download-artifact@v4` with `merge-multiple: true` merges artifacts with the same file path from multiple artifact names by overwriting. If two shards both write a file named `coverage/lcov.info`, the download merges to a single `coverage/lcov.info` — the last-written shard's file. Use shard-indexed output paths (`coverage/lcov-$SHARD_INDEX.info`) in each shard run and merge them explicitly in the merge job rather than relying on `merge-multiple`.

**#86** [community] Testcontainers Ryuk container reaper requires the Docker socket to be mounted as a volume AND the Ryuk container to have `privileged: true` or appropriate capabilities on rootless Docker. CI runners using rootless Docker (increasingly common for security) find that Ryuk silently fails to clean up containers — they accumulate and eventually exhaust the runner's container quota. Set `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_CONTAINER_PRIVILEGED=true` for rootless Docker, or use `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` with explicit `afterAll(() => container.stop())` cleanup as a fallback.

**#87** [community] Node.js 24's built-in test runner `--experimental-test-coverage` reports branch coverage differently from Istanbul: it counts ternary expression branches as separate branches, but logical `&&`/`||` short-circuit branches are not counted. A test that exercises the `true` branch of `a && b()` but never the `false` (where `b()` is not called) shows 100% branch coverage in Node's V8-based counter but 50% in Istanbul. Teams migrating coverage from Jest/Istanbul to the Node built-in runner may see apparent coverage improvements that are actually measurement differences.

**#88** [community] Turborepo remote cache hits can mask test environment regressions. If `REDIS_URL` is part of the test environment hash but the Redis server version is not (it's external infrastructure, not a file), upgrading Redis in production (from 7.2 to 7.4) does not invalidate the Turborepo cache. Tests that ran against Redis 7.2 get a cache hit and are never re-executed against Redis 7.4. Include a `docker-compose.staging.yml` hash or infrastructure version stamp in the Turborepo task's `env` array to ensure cache invalidation when external dependencies change.

## Cycle 25 — 2026-05-13

### Pattern 1 — Playwright `--test-list` and `--test-list-invert` for Deterministic CI Test Selection

Playwright v1.56 added `--test-list` and `--test-list-invert` CLI flags that accept a plain-text file containing one test title per line. `--test-list` runs only the listed tests; `--test-list-invert` runs everything except those tests. This is distinct from `--grep` (regex match on title) and `--only-changed` (git-based file diff): `--test-list` enables externally-generated test selection where a separate script decides which tests to run, such as a risk-scoring model, a flakiness quarantine list, or a dependency-graph tool that maps changed source files to specific test titles rather than whole spec files.

Common CI use case: a nightly script analyzes historical pass/fail data and emits a `slow-tests.txt` file. The PR pipeline runs with `--test-list-invert slow-tests.txt` to exclude long-running tests, then the nightly pipeline runs with `--test-list slow-tests.txt` to run only those tests. This cleanly separates PR and nightly test sets without maintaining two separate config files or two sets of grep patterns.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/playwright-selective.yml
# Demonstrates --test-list and --test-list-invert for split PR / nightly pipelines
name: Playwright Selective

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'   # nightly at 02:00 UTC

jobs:
  generate-test-list:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      slow_tests_exist: ${{ steps.check.outputs.exists }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: check
        run: |
          # Script reads test timing data and emits slow-tests.txt
          # slow-tests.txt: one test full title per line, e.g.:
          #   "checkout flow > payment > stripe timeout handling"
          node scripts/generate-slow-test-list.mjs --threshold-ms=10000 \
            > slow-tests.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "" > slow-tests.txt
          echo "exists=$([ -s slow-tests.txt ] && echo true || echo false)" \
            >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: slow-tests-list
          path: slow-tests.txt
          retention-days: 7

  playwright-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: generate-test-list
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install chromium --with-deps
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { name: slow-tests-list }
      # Exclude slow tests from PR pipeline: fast feedback in < 10 min
      - name: Run fast tests only
        run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --test-list-invert slow-tests.txt \
            --reporter=github,html
        env:
          CI: 'true'

  playwright-nightly:
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    needs: generate-test-list
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version-file: .nvmrc, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { name: slow-tests-list }
      # Run only slow tests during nightly window
      - name: Run slow tests only
        run: |
          npx playwright test \
            --test-list slow-tests.txt \
            --reporter=github,html \
            --retries=1
        env:
          CI: 'true'
```

**Tradeoff:** `--test-list` requires exact test title matches including the full `describe` path. If a developer renames a `test()` or `describe()` block, the list entry becomes a no-op — no error, no skip notice, the test simply does not run. Add a CI validation step that compares the slow-tests list against the current test inventory (`npx playwright test --list`) and fails if any list entry matches zero tests.
